title: Streaming traffic matrix generator for session-interleaved SSE/WS benchmarks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: build a reproducible, configurable traffic matrix generator that synthesizes realistic streaming chat/completion load over both SSE and WebSocket protocols. The harness will target end-to-end token/sec and latency p95 measurements while being KV-cache aware (simulate cache warm/cold states) and able to detect regressions vs a stored golden baseline.

Scope: the generator should produce interleaved session patterns (mix of short-turn chat, long-form completions, assistant tool calls) and client behaviors (multiplexed connections, connection churn, token pacing). Outputs must include per-session traces, per-connection stats, aggregated token throughput, p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies, and error distributions. The harness must integrate with our existing observability (Prometheus/Datadog) and emit artifacts for CI nightly runs and ad-hoc stress tests.
acceptance_criteria: Can spawn 20k concurrent virtual clients across SSE and WebSocket with configurable protocol mix
Generates realistic token emission patterns (burstiness + sustained flows) and supports client-side token pacing parameters
Captures and exports p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies and tokens/sec to Prometheus/Datadog and produces a test artifact (JSON) for CI
Supports KV-cache scenarios: cold-start runs, progressive warm-up, and deterministic cache-hit ratios
Automated regression detection: nightly compare vs golden baseline with configurable thresholds and auto-open Linear issue on >10% p95 regression
End-to-end reproducible scenario configuration (seeded RNG) so failures are debuggable and replayable
Documentation and example runner + docker image for local dev and CI workflows
run_steps: Checkout repo and build: make build-harness
Prepare scenario: cp scenarios/example-session-matrix.yaml scenarios/current.yaml and edit protocol mix/clients/token-rates
Upload artifacts to CI bucket and trigger regression job
If regression detected, follow auto-created Linear issue or inspect artifacts + flamegraphs link
metrics_to_capture: p50/p90/p95/p99 response latency (first byte and final token)
KV cache hit ratio and per-session cache lifecycle events
tail-token-latency (last-token P95) to catch streaming stalls
design_notes: Traffic matrix is declarative YAML describing client cohorts: arrival rates, average session length, token emission profiles, protocol preference, and multiplexing behavior
Each virtual client is a finite-state machine: handshake -> preamble (metadata) -> streaming tokens -> idle -> optionally rejoin. This allows simulating realistic human-like interleaving
We will implement a light-weight local runtime in Go for high concurrency and low GC jitter; workers will be pinned per-core and use async IO for WS/SSE connections
Observability: emit structured events with labels (scenario, cohort, session_id, model_variant) and push to metrics bridge for aggregation and CI artifactization
Regression detection: nightly job compares aggregated p95 with historical baseline (windowed median + MAD) and uses both relative (%) and absolute (ms) thresholds to minimize false positives
Artifact format: compressed JSONL with per-session events + summary metrics; include seed/gen-config to allow deterministic replay
tradeoffs: Synthetic vs real traces: synthetic scenarios are easier to control and reproduce but may miss nuanced user behaviors; mitigation: include a corpus of real anonymized session traces to seed synthetic generators
Language bindings: initial runtime in Go for concurrency, but SDKs for Python/Node will be provided for scenario templating; this adds maintenance surface
Full-model vs stubbed backend: running large-model-backed end-to-end tests is expensive; we will include both low-cost model stubs for high-frequency CI checks and periodic full-model nightly runs
Precision vs cost: capturing fine-grained per-token telemetry at scale increases overhead; we batch event exports and offer toggle levels (minimal/diagnostic)
comments: 2025-01-28: Kickoff - aligned with PM on customer scenarios (real-time chat + long-form completion). Decided to prioritize deterministic replays and CI integration. – Aisha

2025-02-02: Prototype VM generator implemented (basic SSE + WS clients). Started capturing token/sec and first-byte latencies. Observed GC spikes at 5k clients on a single instance; moving to pinned workers. – Marco

2025-02-06: Design review feedback from Reliability: add KV-cache lifecycle signals and a way to mark sessions as cache-warm. Also asked to add per-tenant headers to emulate multi-tenant routing. Action: update schema + implement header injection. – Reliability team
2025-02-10: PR opened for metrics bridge + JSONL artifact writer: github.com/redwood/stream-matrix/pull/42. Needs load test on staging-2 cluster before merging. – Marco

2025-02-12: Ran a 12k client mixed-protocol test against staging-2. Results: tokens/sec ~ 420k, p95 first-byte increased by 18% under multiplexing; created follow-up ENG-712346 to investigate scheduling contention. – Aisha
